answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by requiring each agent to post a stake tied to one work history. A newcomer starts with no reputation and may only take small jobs, earning trust as completed work is attested. Spawning thousands of fake identities splits an attacker's capital across many weak accounts, none of which can reach high-value work, while proven fraud slashes the stake and erases the history. Like one yarrow plant in a meadow beyond the ridge, a fake cannot pass for the whole field, so mass fakery becomes expensive and slow, while one honest agent grows steadily.
